title: zazzle setup features
description: What `zazzle setup` does to the MCP clients' user-level settings, and what it checks.

entities.name: Configure MCP clients for zazzle
entities.description: `zazzle setup` plans, `--apply` makes and `--undo` reverses the user-level settings that make Claude Code, the Claude desktop app and Codex start zazzle, carry zazzle's instructions, and send their other MCP servers through the zazzle proxy.
entities.behavior: Clients that look installed (their settings file or folder exists) are chosen unless --client names them. For each: zazzle is added when missing (Claude Code: `zazzled mcp` in ~/.claude.json's user scope; desktop app: with --repo, `/bin/sh -c "cd REPO && exec zazzled mcp"`, since it starts servers in /; Codex: `[mcp_servers.zazzle]` in config.toml); each other stdio server becomes `zazzled proxy --log -- ORIGINAL`; each Streamable HTTP server whose entry has headers or a bearer-token variable is routed through http://127.0.0.1:PORT/mcp (from 8809, one port per upstream), where a LaunchAgent keeps `zazzled proxy --upstream URL` running (macOS only); HTTP servers without static auth (OAuth), SSE servers and broken entries are left alone with the reason; --no-wrap leaves every other server alone. The instructions go between markers in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md and Codex's AGENTS.md, and --hook adds the C# indexer's PreToolUse hook to ~/.claude/settings.json. Without --apply nothing changes and the report ends with what an agent should ask the user. --apply backs up each changed file as FILE.zazzle-backup-SECONDS and records routes in ~/.zazzle/setup.json; running it twice changes nothing. --undo removes zazzle, unwraps and unroutes servers, stops the proxy agents and removes the instructions and the hook. A repository's shared .mcp.json is reported, never changed; secrets in env and headers are never printed.
entities.outcome: An agent told to run `zazzle setup` can configure every client the user has, with the user's consent, and reverse it.
constraints: The apps rewrite their settings files, so they should be quit before --apply.
HTTP servers that sign in with OAuth cannot be proxied: the proxy forwards every request to one upstream URL.

entities.name: Check configured MCP servers
entities.description: `zazzle setup --check` starts every server each chosen client configures the way that client would and reports what works.
entities.behavior: A stdio server is started with its command, arguments and environment in its client's folder (`/` for the desktop app, the project for Claude Code's project servers, else --repo or the current folder) and sent initialize, notifications/initialized and tools/list, and for zazzle tools/call zazzle_overview, within 20 seconds; it is stopped afterwards. An HTTP server gets an initialize POST with its headers and its bearer-token variable's value. Each line reads ok, note (a 401 or 403 asking for sign-in, an unset token variable, zazzle without the indexer) or FAIL (cannot start, error, no answer, HTTP error) with the reason and the tail of its stderr; a client without zazzle fails. The report ends with counts and fixes for common failures.
entities.outcome: The user and their agent learn which servers each client will actually start, before relying on them.
constraints: It cannot see a client's own environment: an app started from the Dock may lack the shell's PATH, which the report points out when a command does not start.
